reason: The public information architecture is coherent and the Precision Instrument presentation is carefully composed in the supplied mobile and desktop captures. Cost and semester length now appear beside the main actions. I traced the student journey from Join through preparation, evaluation criteria, recruitment availability and the appropriate application/contact action, and the client path from Work terms to the inquiry form. Source and passing local assertions support the corrected outage/no-cycle/empty-event distinctions; the earlier unsupported publication claim is resolved. Mobile organization selection now places the response adjacent. Public canonical/social metadata, private noindex defaults and request-time project detail/image reads are sensible; the publication script exercises synthetic publish/image/withdraw behavior. However, the two main audiences still lack essential decision evidence: an inspectable approved engagement and current membership obligations. Truthful pending disclosures improve trust but do not complete those tasks. Those material information gaps prevent my unqualified world-class agreement. Hosted acceptance remains unknown, so this is not a production release endorsement. I did not observe human task success or operate an authenticated account.

findings.evidence: The committed approved project list is empty. The actual captured homepage presents past partnerships and pending approval; selected profiles explicitly withhold scope, methods, deliverables and outcomes. No approved engagement artifact is supplied. The revised headings accurately describe this limitation.
findings.userImpact: Clients can assess terms and affiliations but cannot inspect comparable MECG reasoning or a handoff before investing in an inquiry.
findings.suggestedFix: Obtain client and Board approval for one bounded engagement with its actual decision, methods, contribution, redacted deliverable and limitations; publish through the existing boundary. Preserve pending disclosure until approved.

findings.evidence: The FAQ explicitly says expected weekly hours, mandatory meeting times and peak commitments are unpublished, and supplies a direct Board email link. This truthfully mitigates the original omission but leaves the substantive answer absent.
findings.userImpact: Students still need a separate conversation to determine whether membership fits their semester.
findings.suggestedFix: Have recruitment leadership approve and date a current-cycle weekly range, required meetings and peak-period expectations, then publish them in this FAQ. Do not invent hours.

notVerified: Hosted Clerk/Supabase/RLS/storage/Resend integration, real sessions and consequential operator recovery; no staging exists.
